page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-192-metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor. The system provides 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated virtual CPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 512 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators, requiring remote block storage for persistent data needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory performance across compute-intensive tests. The instance scored 160,627.1 on multi-core stress-ng tests and achieved 124,318.48 on the PassMark CPU evaluation, placing both in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 463.59 GB/sec alongside 190.86 GB/sec write bandwidth, reflecting the capabilities of the DDR5 subsystem. Dedicated hardware support for AVX-512, AMX int8, and VAES enables high scores in CPU encryption and extended instruction tests. Application-level tests reflect top-tier results in static web serving throughput at 126.66 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 184.72 million operations per second, though single-core execution speed and text processing rank closer to average across tested baselines.

The bare-metal architecture delivers dedicated physical hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead, optimizing core efficiency for intensive multi-threaded tasks. Because local storage is absent, architectures requiring fast disk I/O must factor in remote storage latencies. The instance profile delivers high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it well matched for parallel compilation, ray tracing, web serving at scale, in-memory caching layers, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-192-metal is a compute-focused bare-metal server driven by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs at 4.0 GHz, and 512 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 2.67 GB of memory per core. The platform features no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators. In performance testing, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-threaded processing power, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 160,627.1 and a PassMark CPU score of 124,318.48. Memory bandwidth reaches 463.59 GB/sec for large-block reads, supported by hardware-level AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. The lack of hypervisor overhead maximizes core utilization, although all persistent file operations depend entirely on network-attached storage. This profile matches high-throughput parallel compute workloads, large-scale software compilation, Redis key-value caching, and static web serving.
